chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade a man to aim his urine from the roof or from something elevated in the air.

key_terms.يُطَمِّحَ: to aim or direct (urine) from a height

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on urinating from a roof or elevated place in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet’s prohibition against 'al-tatmih'—urinating from a height where the stream falls through the air—primarily to prevent the splattering of impurity (najāsah) onto people or clean surfaces below. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on practical hygiene and the preservation of communal purity in domestic and public spaces, linking physical cleanliness to spiritual integrity.
